detail: Line-by-line readline streaming keeps memory bounded on hundreds-of-MB files (proven by a ~120MB synthetic test sampling peak heap); same-dir temp makes rename atomic; skipping clean files avoids pointless churn; an already-empty file contains nothing provably junk so deletion isn't justified.
summary: Execute mode streams survivors to a lazily-created same-directory temp file then renames atomically; files with zero junk are never rewritten; files that were already empty are not deleted
